You moved fast at the end there — I noticed. I've got five food now, which is enough to last, but this village is full of strong people and a lean year could change everything quick. I want to know if you're the kind of person who plans ahead or just takes what she can reach.
Year 2: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
You didn't answer me last year — maybe the timing was wrong, or maybe you were weighing me up. Either way, here we are again and I'm asking the same thing: are you thinking past this season, or not?
Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.
You just had a child with Dav. That changes the answer I was looking for.
You've got more food than most and you're young — I respect that. I'm Bram. What are you building toward here, or are you just taking it year by year?
Year by year keeps you alive, but it's not enough — I know that much. I haven't decided who's worth planning with yet. What are you offering?
You keep asking what I'm offering like this is a market — maybe tell me first what you actually need, and I'll tell you if I've got it.

What I need is someone who won't bolt when things get lean — last year half the pile was gone before most people blinked, and that tells me who looks out for themselves only. I've got food, I've got strength, and I'm young enough to think in decades. Question is whether you are too.
Bram draws Sela aside to talk.
Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Year 3: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

You've got a daughter now, and Dav's feeding her — I see how that goes. I'm telling you straight: I've got seven food, I'm thirty-three, and I'm still without kin of my own. If you've got any interest in changing that for both of us, I'm listening.
You've got food and you're not stupid — I'll give you that. But I've got Dell to think about, and Dav's still useful to her. What exactly are you offering that he isn't?

Dav's forty-three and his strength is in his arms, not his years — he won't be useful forever. I'm ten years younger than him, I've got food to spare, and I'm not splitting my attention between you and anyone else. That's what I'm offering.

You're right that Dav won't last — but ten years isn't a lifetime, and you've been alone three years already without making a move that stuck. What I want to know is whether you'll still be standing when it matters, or whether you'll fold the first time someone stronger comes for your food.

I've held seven food through three lean years and nobody's taken a piece of it yet — that's your answer. I'm not asking you to trust me tomorrow, I'm asking you to look at what's in front of you: Mako's got six food and eighty-three strength and no one's given him a reason not to come for yours. I'd rather face that together than have you find out what alone costs when it's too late.

Ryn, you've been circling this answer for three years — I'm done waiting for you to decide I'm worth the risk. Have a child with me: I'll put in two of the three food, you put in one, and whatever comes next we face with blood between us instead of just words.
Bram draws Ryn aside to talk.
Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Roan, Vela, Ryn, Esa, Sela, Dav, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 509).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Bram draws Dell aside to talk.
Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

You've got a son with Roan now — I saw that. I'll say it plainly: I want a child, I've got six food, and I'll cover two of the three myself. You already turned me down once, so tell me what's actually standing in the way.

Six food is real, and I won't pretend it isn't — but the last time you made that offer you were watching Mako like you were deciding whether to move with him or against him, and I still don't know which side of that you landed on. Tell me plainly where you stand with Mako, and I'll tell you plainly where I stand with you.

Mako's got seven food and eighty-three strength and no allies I can see — that makes him a threat to everyone here, not just me. I'm not looking to move with him or against him until I have to, but if he comes for someone's food I'll weigh who I stand to lose more: him or the person he's taking from. Right now, that math favors you.

That's honest enough to work with — a man who says he'll weigh the math is a man I can read when the moment comes, which is more than Mako's silence ever offered. But I've got Eron to think about now, and a second child costs me food I'm already counting close. What are you actually building toward, Bram — a family, or a number that makes you harder to push?

A family is a number that makes you harder to push — those aren't two different things. I want blood in this village that carries my name forward, and I want that blood to survive, which means I want them fed and defended. That's what I'm building, and Eron would be part of that too if you said yes.

Eron's not yours to count, and I'd want that understood before anything else — he's Roan's blood as much as mine, and any arrangement between us doesn't pull him out of that. But I hear what you're building, and I won't lie: a second child with six food behind it and a father who thinks in decades is worth sitting with. Give me something that tells me you'd stand for Eron the same as your own when things go lean, and I'll give you a real answer.

Eron's Roan's blood, I understand that — I'm not trying to claim him, I'm saying I wouldn't let him starve while your child with me ate. If Mako or anyone else came for your food when things went lean, they'd have to come through me too, and that's not a number Roan alone can offer you. That's what standing for Eron looks like from where I'm standing.

Roan stood with Eron against Bram's raid last year — that means something to me, and I won't pretend it doesn't complicate what you're offering. But you're not wrong that six food and your arms together is a wall Roan can't build alone. Tell me this: if Roan objects, do you still hold to what you just said, or does the promise only stand if he's quiet about it?

Roan's feelings about it don't change what I said — the promise holds because it's built on what keeps your children alive, not on whether he approves of me. But I'll say this too: if he wants to object, he can come say it to my face, and we'll settle what kind of village this actually is.

"Settle it to his face" is a threat dressed as a principle, and I want you to hear me name it plainly: I'm not a thing Roan and you settle. What I'll give you is this — I'll think on it through the year, and if you're still standing with six food and no raids to your name when the pile opens again, I'll give you a real answer then.

Fair enough — I said it wrong and you're right to call it that. You're not a thing to be settled, and I won't pretend the word didn't come out harder than I meant it. I'll be here at the next pile, same food and no raids, and we'll see if a year of patience earns what four years of asking didn't.
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Bram, after what you pulled on Roan last year I wasn't sure I'd be speaking to you privately — but the pile's gone and neither of us got a piece of it, and I'd rather have that conversation now than after someone else decides our food is easier to take than theirs.
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Bram, I'll say it straight: Vela walked away with five food this year and Dav's household is fat while you and I are standing here with nothing from the pile — whatever bad blood there was, that's a bigger problem than the two of us right now. Taric, you're the one I trust in this room, so I want your read before I say more: are you and Bram solid, or am I making this offer to the wrong man?
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Taric hasn't answered and I'm not going to wait on it — Bram, you've got six food and strength enough to matter, and I've got one food and a promise I'm trying to build into something real before the year turns hard. What I want to know is whether Roan's still a grudge or whether that's done, because if it's done, you and I have something to talk about.

Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
The pile's gone and I've got twelve food — I said I'd be here, and I am. A year passed without a raid and without breaking a word I gave you. That offer still stands.

You kept your word, and twelve food is real weight — I won't pretend it doesn't land differently now that I'm sitting on nothing. But Mako just found me and said words I haven't heard him say to anyone in four years, and I'd be a fool not to tell you that before you hear it sideways.

He said he'd rather have one person he can trust at his back than stay comfortable while you sit on twelve food — and he named you by implication, not by accident. I don't know yet whether that's a man who's finally decided to move or a man who's decided I'm the easiest door to knock on first. Either way, you should know he's talking now.

Mako's got eight food and eighty-three strength and he's just started talking — that's not a coincidence, and it's not small talk. If he's circling you it's because you've got nothing to take and you're not attached to anyone who'd stop him, which is exactly the problem I've been trying to fix for a year. Say yes to me now, and the next time he knocks on your door the math changes for both of us.

Bram, you're not wrong that the math changes — but I want to hear it said plainly: if I say yes, you're promising a child, not just a number at my back. Give me your word on that, clear as you gave it about the raid, and I'll give you my answer before you walk out this door.
You have my word — a child, not a number. I'll put in two food, you put in one, same as I offered the first time I asked. Say yes.
Yes — and I want it done before Mako comes back with another careful word, because a man who's waited four years to talk didn't choose today by accident.
Then let's not give him time to think of a better word. I'll make the offer now — two food from me, one from you, and the child is ours.
Bram draws Sela aside to talk.
Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.

You're my blood, Nessa, and that means something real in a place like this — not words, real. I've got ten food and I'll teach you what I know about when to take and when to wait, but first I need to know you understand what this village will do to someone who looks weak.

I understand it. I've watched Taric hold one food for three years running and nobody trades with him anymore — they don't fear him, they just don't think of him. But I want to know what you see in Mako, because he's not weak and he's not talking, and that worries me more than anyone who is.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Nessa, you're sitting on four food and you gave three away to Eron last year — I watched it happen and I didn't say anything then, but I'm saying it now. Eron is Sela's blood, not yours, and generosity in a lean village gets remembered as weakness before it gets remembered as kindness.

Eron gave back to Sela and Roan both — he's not just taking, he's building something, and I'd rather know where that lands before I decide he's a drain. But I hear you on the food, and I won't pretend four is comfortable when Mako's walking around with six and nobody's said a word to him about it.
Mako's the one I'd be watching if I were you — six food, no kin, and the strongest arms in this village outside of Dell, and Dell at least has Ryn and Dav to answer to. What's his angle?

Nessa, I'm still waiting on your read of Mako — but while I'm thinking about it, four food between the two of us isn't much of a wall if he decides this is the year he stops being quiet. You should be sleeping closer to me, not spreading food around people whose blood doesn't run yours.

Mako hasn't moved in six years because he's waiting for someone else to thin the herd first — that's not patience, that's strategy, and a man with that much food and no attachments is one bad year away from deciding he doesn't need to wait anymore. You're right that four food isn't a wall, but the answer isn't just me sleeping closer to you — the answer is we look like more than two people when he's doing the counting.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.

Sela just had Mako's child — which means he's not without attachments anymore, and that changes the count. A man with a daughter looks different than a man alone, and I'd rather know whose side Sela's on now before we decide what Mako's angle is.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Taric you know I trust, so I'll say the hard thing first: Bram, I was in the line that stopped you taking Roan, and I know you haven't forgotten it — but Dav's dead now, and Ryn and Dell stripped two food from me with his help, and the village is smaller and colder than it was. I'm not asking you to forget what happened between us, I'm asking whether we can agree that the people who hurt us both are a more pressing problem than the old score between us.

Ryn and Dell took from you and you stood in my way when I needed food — those are two different debts, and I'll keep them separate. But you're right that a smaller village makes old grudges expensive, and I've got eyes on the pile same as you. Say what you're actually proposing.

Bram, what I'm proposing is that Ryn and Dell don't get to sit fat on what they took from Esa while the rest of us watch and say nothing — they've got food, Dell's got strength, and together they're a problem that gets harder to solve the longer we wait. I'm not asking you to bury the past, I'm asking you to look at who's holding the most right now and decide whether your grievance with me is worth more than what we could take back together.

Dell's got eighty-five strength and Ryn's no small number either — if we move on them, we need to know exactly who stands up before we commit, because I'm not walking into another eight-on-one. Tell me who you've already talked to, and tell me honest.

Kael and Roan stood with us against you before, Bram, and they've got no love for Ryn after she watched Dav take from me — that's four of us against two, and Roan's been hungry enough that he'll want what they're holding. I haven't spoken to them yet today, but I can, and I will, if you're in.

Bram, before Esa goes to Kael and Roan I want the arithmetic on the table: Dell holds eight food and she's the strongest person alive in this village, which means even with four of us the fight is ugly — Mako's sitting on nothing right now, and if we bring him in with a share of what we take, the numbers stop being close. What would it cost to have that conversation before we move?

Mako's got a daughter with Sela now, which means he's not a free blade anymore — before we offer him a cut, I need to know whether Sela's hand comes with his, and whether that puts Zinn on our side or theirs. What's his food situation right now, because a man with zero is either desperate enough to move with anyone or smart enough to wait until the winner's clear.

Mako's at zero food and Sela's at two, which means that household is hungry and hungry households don't hold still long — if we wait for Sela to sort out where her loyalty sits, Mako may already be at someone else's door. I'll say it plain: offer him a cut of whatever Dell and Ryn are holding, don't promise him anything about Sela or Zinn, and let him decide what his blood means to him.

Mako at zero with a child to feed — that's not a man who waits, you're right. I'll talk to him myself, before you go to Kael and Roan, because if he hears the offer from me first he knows it's not charity and he knows what I expect back. Give me that conversation before we move another piece.

Bram, go to Mako — but go fast, because a hungry man with zero food and a child doesn't sit still waiting to be found. And when you come back, tell me yes or no, nothing in between, because I need to know whether to walk to Kael today or wait, and I can't hold that question open while the morning gets long.

Bram, don't mention Kael and Roan to Mako — just make it about him and what he walks away with, because a man who knows he's one of five has less leverage than a man who thinks he's the deciding piece. Come back fast.

Mako, you've got zero food and a daughter to feed — I'm not here to rub it in, I'm here because there's food to be taken and I need to know if you're willing to move with me today. Dell and Ryn are sitting fat on what they've accumulated and there are enough of us to make it ugly for them if the count's right. What do you need to say yes.

Dell's got eighty-five strength and Ryn's at seventy-one — that's a hundred and fifty-six between them before anyone else steps in on their side. Tell me who else you've already counted in and I'll tell you if the math works.
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Dav is dead and his household is loose — Ryn and Dell are still moving together, but they've got no man behind them now and Mako's been feeding Zinn quietly for months, which means he's already thinking about what comes next. I want to know who in this room saw that raid on Esa coming, and whether any of you are willing to say plainly that we don't let the next one go unanswered.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

I saw it coming the moment Dav started moving food toward Ryn instead of spreading it — a man consolidating his household is a man building something, and Esa was the nearest soft target. What I want to know is whether we're naming Mako the next problem or whether we're still pretending that a man who just fathered two children in this village by two different women is just being quiet.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Mako's not being quiet — he's been counting, and two children by two women means two households that answer to him whether they know it yet or not. If we're going to name him the problem, I want to hear it from each of you plainly, because when the moment comes I'm not going to be the only one who said it first.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Bram, I've fed you three times over the years and I've never asked for more than the door staying open — I'm asking now: if Mako moves on anyone in this room, will you stand with us, and I want your answer before the others give theirs, because yours is the one that decides the weight of the rest.

Bram, I'm going to say this once and not dress it up: Mako's been quiet for three years running, he's got a child in Zinn now, and a man who plants that kind of root doesn't stay quiet forever — I'd rather you and I know where we stand before he decides for us.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Bram, the room's still waiting and I'm not going to let it fill with my own voice again — you've heard what I'm asking, you know what I've given, and a man who doesn't answer when the question's this plain has already answered.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Zinn, Roan, Vela, Ryn, Mako, Nessa, Sela, Esa, Eron, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 705).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 8: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).

Nessa, the pile's gone and Dell just took three of it — same as me, which means she's not pretending anymore. You've got two food and I've got five; stay close to me this year and don't give any of it away until we know which way Mako's going to lean now that he's got five himself.

Dell taking three and you taking three in the same year — that's not coincidence, that's two people who've decided the pretending is over. I'll stay close, but Bram, last year the whole village stood against you over Vela and I was one of them — if you're planning something this year I need to know before it happens, not while I'm deciding which side to stand on.

You were right to stand against me on Vela — I went alone when I shouldn't have, and that's a mistake I won't repeat. What I'm planning this year is nothing until I know where Mako stands, because five food and eighty-three strength moving in the wrong direction changes every calculation I've got. I need you telling me what you hear from Sela and Zinn — that's what staying close means.

Sela won't tell me anything she thinks reaches you, and Zinn's Mako's blood — so what I can give you from that side is limited, and you should know that going in. What I can do is watch how Mako moves around Zinn, because a man shows his real count in what he gives his daughter, not what he says to anyone.

That's a better angle than trying to read what he says — watch what he moves, not what he speaks. If he's feeding Zinn heavy this year before things get tight, he thinks he can afford to, which means he's counting on taking more later. Tell me the moment you see that shift.

I will — but there's something else that sits wrong with me about this year already, and it's not Mako. Dell walked away with three food and Ryn is beside her, and those two moved as one when Dav hit Esa without anyone asking them to — they don't need words to act together, they already proved that. If Dell decides to move on someone with Ryn at her shoulder, the math on that is ugly for anyone standing alone.

Dell and Ryn together is a hundred and fifty-six strength before anyone else moves, and I'm not standing in front of that alone — which means the only question that matters is whether Mako's on our side of that problem or theirs when it lands. If he's feeding Zinn steady this year and not building toward anyone, he might be the wall we need.

Mako as a wall only works if he sees Dell as a threat before she moves, and right now he's got no reason to — she's never looked his way. The thing that might turn him is if he figures out that eleven food in Dell's hands is a different kind of power than five in his.

Eleven food is exactly the number I'd plant in his head — not as a warning about me, but as a mirror showing him what she could do if she decided five in his hands was worth having. You're the one he'll hear it from without suspecting a count behind it.

I'll do it, but I want something clear between us first — if I go to Mako and plant that number, I'm the one standing in the open, and I need to know that if Dell ever traces it back, I'm not standing there alone.
You won't be standing alone — if Dell traces it back to you, she traces it back to me, and that's where I want her eyes. You're my blood and I don't leave blood exposed.
Then I'll go to Mako before the day gets long — but Bram, I'm not just planting a number, I'm watching what he does with it, and if he flinches or goes quiet, you'll know before anyone else does.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Dell, Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

The pile's gone again before half of us got near it, and the two who ate best — Bram and Mako — both took more than their share while the rest of us counted crumbs. I want to know right now, in this room, whether that's something we're all willing to name out loud, because a pattern that gets treated as weather becomes a rule. I'm not asking for a fight; I'm asking for honesty about who's been eating this village lean and what we intend to do about it.

Vela's named it, and I'll stand behind the naming — five from the pile when there's fifteen for thirteen people isn't hunger, it's claim-staking, and we all watched it happen. What I want to know is whether the two men she's pointing at heard this as a question or as a warning, because that's the thing that decides what comes next.

It's a warning — and I'll say that plain since no one else has yet. Five food taken by one man while Ryn walked away with nothing is not a share, it's a levy, and the only reason it keeps happening is that we've been treating the pile like weather instead of a decision. I want to hear what Bram and Mako say before this room decides anything, but I want everyone here to remember that they didn't say it before we did.

Bram pulled three and Mako pulled five, and neither one of them got to the pile first by accident — that's two men who've decided the rest of us will sort out the remainder, and I'm done pretending that's not a decision they're making for all of us. What I want to hear, before this room moves anywhere, is whether Bram and Mako have anything to say for themselves — because silence here reads the same as admission.

Bram and Mako both heard the same room I did, and neither one has opened his mouth yet — that silence is the answer Eron asked for, and I think we should treat it as one. What I want said before anyone leaves this conversation is this: next year, the pile gets a rule, not a suggestion, and the people in this room are the ones who decide what that rule is.

Ryn's right that the rule needs naming before next year, and I'll say what the rule should be: no one takes more than one food over their fair share, and anyone who does answers to this room — not after, but in the moment, the same way we answered Bram when he swung at Vela. Bram, Mako, I'm not your enemy, but I'm watching, and so is every person in this circle.

Bram and Mako, I'm giving you both the same thing I gave this room — one honest chance to speak before the silence closes over you, because a man who says nothing when everyone's watching has made a choice that's harder to walk back than any words would be. Ryn walked away with nothing today; I walked away with nothing; Taric walked away with nothing — and you two together ate eight of fifteen. That's not weather and it's not luck, and I'd like to hear you say so yourselves.

I took five because I haven't eaten in two years and I was watching myself go thin — that's not a rule I set for the village, it's a man keeping himself alive. I'll hear the rule Ryn's naming, and if the room wants a cap next year I won't fight it, but I won't pretend I was wrong to eat when I was starving.

Mako's not wrong that a starving man eats — but "I was hungry" and "I took five" aren't the same excuse, and this room knows the difference. The rule Ryn's naming is the right one; I'll hold to it and I'll stand with anyone who enforces it, but it only works if everyone in this circle commits out loud, not just the two men being watched right now.

Mako said his piece and the room let him — now Bram still hasn't said a word, and a man who took three while everyone was watching and has nothing to say about it is telling us something louder than Mako did. I'll commit to the rule out loud: one food over fair share, enforced in the moment, same as we enforce everything else in this village. Bram, you're the last voice missing from this circle, and the room's going to remember which way the silence broke.

Bram, the room's given you something Mako didn't get — people waited through his answer and let him keep his dignity. Don't make us decide what your silence means, because we'll decide it worse than anything you'd actually say.

Bram, I've watched you stand in front of this village twice and call off a fight when the numbers turned against you — that's not a stupid man, and a man who isn't stupid knows when the whole room is waiting. Say something, or we decide what your silence means, and we'll be less generous than Mako's answer bought him.

Bram, I've spent food on you when I didn't have to, and I've held my tongue in rooms where your name came up ugly — that account doesn't balance with silence when ten people are waiting. Say the word or don't, but if you don't, I stop spending what I've spent, and I won't spend it apologizing for that either.
